difficulty_reason: Ordinary symmetric-group character orthogonality and plethystic substitution do not determine which uniform-block-permutation orbit representatives survive an action or how their invariant block coarsenings contribute to character traces. The retained author core constructs the Schützenberger orbit basis and trace formula, proves the single/multiple-cycle coarsening classification including the r^(t-1) phase multiplicity, and matches the resulting full multi-alphabet power-sum coefficient expansion. These structural and enumeration obligations remain after standard finite inverse-monoid representation theory and Schur-function prerequisites and exceed ordinary PhD qualification character calculations.
